::: {.lead}
`resid` builds a dated equity universe, computes factor exposures,
estimates daily factor returns, and exports the unexplained component as
residual return.
:::

## Setup

Install [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/getting-started), clone marcap next to
this repository, then install Python 3.14 and the locked dependencies:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/FinanceData/marcap.git ../marcap
mise install
uv sync
```

## CLI

The evaluated command uses:

- a daily top-1,000 universe selected from the previous close;
- sequential OLS over MKT, SMB, HML, and MOM; and
- coverage, finite-output, reconstruction, and orthogonality checks.

```bash
uv run resid \
  --data-dir ../marcap/data \
  --output-dir output/full \
  --universe-method daily \
  --output-years 10 \
  --universe-size 1000 \
  --momentum-lookback-days 189 \
  --momentum-skip-days 63 \
  --momentum-min-periods 126 \
  --value-lookback-days 1008 \
  --value-skip-days 252 \
  --value-min-periods 756 \
  --market-beta \
  --market-beta-lookback-days 252 \
  --market-beta-min-periods 126 \
  --market-beta-decay 0.97 \
  --regression-method ols \
  --winsor-quantile 0.01 \
  --minimum-date-coverage 0.99 \
  --validation-tolerance 1e-12
```

Omit `--end-date` to use the latest local observation. Use
`--universe-method fixed` for a first-day snapshot. See every option with
`uv run resid --help`.

### Outputs

The CSV files use standard factor-model notation:

| Notation | File | Contents | Schema |
|---|---|---|---|
| ε | `epsilon.csv` | Specific returns | `(date, ticker, specific_return)` |
| r | `r.csv` | Returns used by the regression | `(date, ticker, return)` |
| X | `X.csv` | Normalized exposures | `(date, ticker, <one column per factor>)` |
| f | `f.csv` | Daily factor returns | `(date, <one column per factor>)` |

`epsilon.csv` is the primary output. The other files support reconstruction
and diagnosis. X and f store `INTERCEPT`, `MKT`, `SMB`, `HML`, and `MOM` in
removal order, with `r = Xf + ε`.

Ticker values are zero-padded strings:

```python
import pandas as pd

epsilon = pd.read_csv("output/full/epsilon.csv", dtype={"ticker": "string"})
```

## Python API

```python
from pathlib import Path

import resid

source = resid.MarcapDataSource(Path("../marcap/data"))
base_model = resid.CharacteristicFactorModel(
    (
        resid.size_factor(name="SMB", small_minus_big=True),
        resid.long_term_reversal_factor(
            lookback_days=1008,
            skip_days=252,
            min_periods=756,
            name="HML",
        ),
        resid.momentum_factor(
            lookback_days=189,
            skip_days=63,
            min_periods=126,
            name="MOM",
        ),
    )
)
factor_model = resid.RecursiveMarketBetaModel(
    base=base_model,
    lookback_days=252,
    min_periods=126,
    decay=0.97,
    name="MKT",
)

result = resid.run_pipeline(
    window=resid.analysis_window(source, years=10, end=None),
    source=source,
    universe_builder=resid.DailyTopMarketCapUniverse(size=1000),
    return_calculator=resid.PercentageReturns(),
    factor_model=factor_model,
    residualizer=resid.SequentialOLSResidualizer(
        factor_order=("MKT", "SMB", "HML", "MOM"),
        winsor_quantile=0.01,
        unscaled_factors=("MKT",),
    ),
    regression_weight_model=resid.EqualRegressionWeights(),
    validations=(
        resid.RegressionCoverageValidation(minimum_date_coverage=0.99),
        resid.FiniteOutputValidation(),
        resid.ReturnReconstructionValidation(absolute_tolerance=1e-12),
        resid.SequentialOrthogonalityValidation(absolute_tolerance=1e-12),
    ),
)
resid.CsvArtifactWriter().write(result, Path("output/full"))
```

Key choices:

- Factor order sets attribution priority; changing it changes the model.
- MKT stays in beta units through `unscaled_factors`; the styles use
  standardized exposures.
- `RecursiveMarketBetaModel` adds stateful beta to the style model. Use the
  style model directly to omit it.
- Sequential WLS and joint OLS are available behind the same residualizer
  boundary.

## Contracts

| Stage output | Contract |
|---|---|
| Market data | DataFrame indexed by `(date, ticker)` with `return_percent` and `market_cap` |
| Universe | Boolean Series indexed by `(date, ticker)` |
| Returns | Series named `return`, indexed by `(date, ticker)` |
| Exposures | DataFrame indexed by `(date, ticker)`, one column per factor |
| Regression weights | Positive Series indexed by `(date, ticker)` |
| Result | `ResidualizationResult` with ε, r, X, f, weights, diagnostics, universe, and validation results |

ty checks the callable interfaces; integration tests cover the DataFrame
schemas.
